paragraphs: Berkshire has no county council, so fostering here is run by six local services: Bracknell Forest Council, Brighter Futures for Children in Reading, Slough Children First, West Berkshire Council, Wokingham Borough Council, and Achieving for Children for Windsor and Maidenhead. The independent agencies shown above also approve carers across the county. Each area has its own page on this site, linked below.

All six are part of Local Authority Fostering South East, the regional hub that Bracknell Forest has led since it launched in July 2024. It gives people one place to make a first enquiry and a fostering ambassador scheme so you can talk to someone who already fosters. Across the South East, the councils said they had more than 11,000 children in care and fewer than 3,000 council-approved carers. Slough Children First said the aim locally was to keep children in or near Slough with the right carers.

Our council pay pages show what two Berkshire services pay for 2026-27. Slough pays the child's allowance, from £195 to £298 a week by age, plus a level-of-care payment of £200 to £300 a week depending on the carer's skills and experience. Bracknell Forest publishes one combined weekly figure for allowance and fee, from £304.83 to £480.34 at its first tier, with extra payments for skills or a child's disability where they apply.

Berkshire falls in the South East band of the national minimum allowance, which for 2026-27 runs from £195 a week for a baby to £298 for a 16 or 17 year old. Speak to your own council and to two or three of the agencies above, and compare training and support as well as pay.
